implementation_notes: Ruby's constant resolution is the lookup service: Object.const_get("Plugins::Render") resolves a (possibly namespaced) constant name to its current value, searching the receiver's ancestors unless inherit is false, and every Module keeps its own constant table as the binding store. Module#autoload registers a name whose first resolution loads the file that defines it - a lazy binding - and const_source_location reports where a binding currently comes from, which makes re-resolution after remove_const or redefinition observable instead of guessed. What replaces the classic structure is the language's per-module constant table plus the load path; a separate lookup service is only needed when the resource is not a Ruby constant.
code_sketch:
module Plugins
  autoload :Render, "plugins/render"        # name -> file, resolved on first use
end

klass  = Object.const_get("Plugins::Render")  # namespaced name -> constant
plugin = klass.new
Plugins.const_source_location(:Render)       # => ["plugins/render.rb", 3]
pitfalls: const_get('Foo::Bar') with a string from untrusted input can reach any loaded constant - name resolution is code-adjacent, so validate names against an allow-list before resolving.
The inherit flag defaults to true, so a name can silently resolve to an ancestor's constant; pass false when the binding must belong to the receiver itself.
A miss raises NameError, but so does a failing autoload lookup inside the resolved file; check const_defined? to distinguish 'no binding' from 'binding is broken'.
